L19: # Grand Canyon National Park • Arizona
L20: 
L21: Entirely within the state of Arizona, the park encompasses 278 miles (447 km) of the Colorado River and adjacent uplands. Located on the ancestral homelands of 11 present day Tribal Communities, Grand Canyon is one of the most spectacular examples of erosion anywhere in the world—a mile deep canyon unmatched in the incomparable vistas it offers visitors from both north and south rims.

L41: cite9†Entrance Fees and Passes L42: 
L43: cite10†Image: A white car at a stone entrance station L44: 
L45: What pass should you pick? A standard or an annual pass? How much do they cost? Do you qualify for a military, senior, or access pass?
L46: 
L47: cite11†South Rim - Lodging and Camping L48: 
L49: cite12†Image: A wooden Swiss chalet lodge.  L50: Note: Overnight lodging currently suspended due to Stage 4 water restrictions. Dry camping still available. The South Rim is open all year.
L51: 
L52: cite13†Today's Key Hiking Messages L53: 
L54: cite14†Image: On a backcountry trail a hiker with a backpack walks uphill.  L55: 
L56: Know before you go! Learn about trail conditions and closures, the weather forecast, and drinking water availability inside the canyon.
L57: 
L58: cite15†What's Open Today? L59: cite16†Image: People walking across a plaza with information kiosks on the left and a long building on the right. L60: 
L61: Here's an updated list of South Rim hours of operation for visitor centers, restaurants, shops, and other services within the park.
L62: 
L63: cite17†Ride the Free South Rim Shuttle Buses L64: 
L65: cite18†Image: A green and white bus at a bus stop with a canyon landscape in the background L66: Park once, then let the buses transport you from Visitor Center parking lots to scenic overlooks, trailheads, and all village services.
L67: 
L68: cite19†Weather, Webcams and Roads L69: 
L70: cite20†Image: two people at a scenic overlook are looking at a vast canyon filled with a cloud inversion.  L71: 
L72: Includes weather forecast maps and graphics. Webcams show current conditions. Road closure updates here—or call 928-638-7496 for recording.
L73: 
L74: cite21†Things To Do L75: cite22†Image: Park Visitors taking photos from standing alongside a guardrail.  L76: 
L77: Walking, hiking, bicycling, touring, stargazing, rail adventures, mule trips, guided learning —or just relaxing and taking in the view.
L78: 
L79: cite23†Programs and Special Events L80: 
L81: cite24†Image: A group of park visitors listening to a ranger talk, with Grand Canyon in the background L82: 
L83: Here's the calendar of this week's ranger and astronomy programs, cultural demonstrations and special events.
L84: 
L85: cite25†Backcountry Camping Permits Are Required L86: cite26†Image: A creek with campsites on one side of the creek and several people with tents L87: 
L88: To camp overnight anywhere inside Grand Canyon you must first obtain a permit from the Backcountry Information Center.
L89: 
L90: cite27†North Rim - OPEN for 2026 Season L91: 
L92: cite28†Image: Landscape seen from Grand Canyon Lodge. Two massive reddish peaks at sunset. L93: 
L94: Select areas of the North Rim have reopened for the 2026 season. Follow this link for more information.
L95: 
L96: cite29†Park Overview L97: cite30†Image: Jagged limestone pillars frame sunset-lit peaks in a vast canyon. L98: 
L99: Fun facts about the geology, geography, climate, history, and the park's natural and cultural resources.
L100: 
L101: cite31†Homeland of Tribal Communities L102: 
L103: cite32†Image: graphic shows names of tribes around a circle with words "Tribes Call the Canyon Home". L104: 
L105: 11 tribes have cultural connections to the lands and resources now found within Grand Canyon National Park.
L106: 
L107: cite33†Special Use Permits (SUP) L108: cite34†Image: Two holding hands during a wedding ceremony with the canyon in the background. L109: 
L110: Special events held within the park like weddings, Rim-to-Rim extended day hikes, and large gatherings require special use permits.
L111: 
L112: cite35†Filming and Photography Permits L113: 
L114: cite36†Image: A ranger is interviewed near the canyon rim with a reporter and a videographer.  L115: 
L116: A special use permit is required for certain filming and still photography activities within the park.
L117: 
L118: cite37†Commercial Use Authorization (CUA) L119: cite38†Image: Two large tour buses and two transit vans are parked in a loading zone. L120: 
L121: CUAs are required for road-based tours, guided backcountry trips and all other commercial activities for visitors within the park.
